O.description: 14 primitive operators from v2.0.2. King Wen uses a subset heavily; some are external-boundary only.

measurement.method: Forward: for each of 64 hexagrams, expand to ternary line states per phase_bits 0-7. Inverse: reconstruct binary from ternary states. Assert all 64 round-trip bit-exact.
files: kingwen_ternary_tables_complete.py:53-72 (PHASE_LINE_MAP — defines which positions become yao per phase_bits)
emotional_engine.py:207-280 (_line_state_balance — computes ternary state per line)

edges.notes: 64 base hexagrams, each with 8 phase variants = 512 reachable ternary representations from 729 possible ternary line-state space. Phase_bits 0-7 selects which lines become yao (changing). Fully deterministic and reversible when phase_bits is known.

measurement.method: Forward: ternary line states → 9-bit index (0-511). Inverse: given 9-bit index, recover ternary line states. Check: multiple ternary states may collapse to same 9-bit index (lossy when only index retained).
files: kingwen_ternary_tables_complete.py:5-6 (64×8=512 total entries; 3^6=729 possible line-state combinations)

edges.notes: Lossy when reduced to only the resolved index — the index doesn't encode which ternary positions produced it. Reversible if full ternary representation is retained alongside the index.

measurement.method: Given an emotional vector (5-axis), find all hexagrams whose _primary_pool_for_hex produces a vector within ε. Expected: many-to-one mapping (lossy).
files: emotional_engine.py:320-341 (_primary_pool_for_hex — derives primary pool from line-state dominance)
emotional_engine.py:283-295 (_trigram_vector — trigram context vector, secondary weighting)

edges.notes: Explicitly lossy: many hexagrams share similar emotional vectors. The vector determines color palette, audio band, mesh palette for downstream consumers — but doesn't uniquely identify the hexagram.

measurement.method: compose_state_key(hex, phase, mask, coherence, porosity) → state_key string. parse_state_key(state_key) → dict. Assert round-trip preserves all fields.

edges.notes: Fully reversible: the state key is a string encoding of the composite state. Both directions are deterministic.

measurement.method: Given a skill card (JSON), recover hexagram_id. Check: skill cards are per-hexagram, so recovery should be unique. But skill card content (category/action/domain) is derived, not reversible to full expansion.

edges.notes: Lossy: skill card content (personality tags, domain, category) is derived from the hexagram's immutable table tags, but the full expansion detail is not recoverable from the card alone.

measurement.method: extract_intent(request_text) → intent_dict with dominant_intent, intent_vector. Inverse: given intent_vector, attempt to reconstruct request_text. Measure overlap.
files: emotional_engine.py:48-64 (_INTENT_KEYWORDS — 12 intent categories with keyword lists)
emotional_engine.py:115-140 (extract_intent — keyword matching + deterministic hash perturbation)
emotional_engine.py:143-200 (_intent_to_vector — maps intent distribution to 5-axis seed)

edges.notes: Deterministic transform (same text → same intent_vector), but lossy recovery (many texts map to same dominant_intent). The hash perturbation in _intent_to_vector adds continuous variation but is deterministic.

measurement.method: Full expansion pipeline: request_text → extract_intent → _pool_weights_for_hex → expand_hexagram → state keys. Inverse: given final state keys, recover request_text.
files: full_hexagram_shotgun.py:1-10 (architecture: query → parse → inject all 64 → expand ternary → personality → downstream)
emotional_engine.py:585-600 (_pool_weights_for_hex — derives pool, porosity, inject metadata from structure + intent)

edges.notes: The full expansion pipeline is deterministic (same request_text → same expansion), but the request_text is not recoverable from the expansion output.

measurement.method: Run same expanded state through Jarvis LLM N times. Measure output variance (e.g., standard deviation of semantic similarity across N runs). Determinism = 0.0 means non-deterministic output.
files: kingwen_oracle_consult_tool.py (boundary between King Wen engine and Jarvis)
External: OpenJarvis agent runtime (consumes expanded states)

edges.notes: This is the phase-transition point: deterministic King Wen computation → stochastic LLM interpretation. Determinism drops from 1.0 to 0.0 at this edge.

measurement.method: Möbius transformation (z - z0) / (z + z0) on complex plane. Forward: state_key → mobius_gamma. Inverse: mobius is its own inverse up to conjugation. Check round-trip.

edges.notes: Möbius is a conformal map; the transformation is deterministic and approximately reversible (Möbius transformations are bijective on the Riemann sphere).

measurement.method: Stereographic projection: sphere point → complex plane → inverse. Forward: state_key → sphere coords → (u,v). Inverse: (u,v) → sphere coords. Check inverse_error ≈ 0.

edges.notes: Stereographic projection and its inverse are exact (conformal). inverse_error should be ≈ 0 (floating-point precision). Fully reversible.

measurement.method: Void null projection: hexagrams 15/20/30/40 → null-state South Pole (radius=0). Inverse: from null state, cannot recover original hexagram (all void hexes map to same null).

edges.notes: Lossy by design: void hexes (15, 20, 30, 40) all map to the same null state (South Pole, radius=0). Cannot recover which void hex produced it. This is intentional — 'bounded absence,' not another phase.

measurement.method: Gaussian future bias: weight future phase (index 2) through Gaussian kernel with FWHM. Forward: state_key → phase_bias vector. Inverse: from phase_bias, recover phase_bits — partially ambiguous due to Gaussian smoothing.

edges.notes: The Gaussian smoothing makes the projection lossy for inverse recovery — multiple phase configurations can produce similar bias vectors.

measurement.method: Identity projection: state_key → same state_key. Trivial round-trip.
Route hexagram to topic based on emotional vector + trainingNotes. Measure: given topic, find hexagrams whose vector aligns. Check correlation decay over distance.

edges.notes: Conceptual routing substrate. The RESONATE edge maps hexagram emotional vectors to topic/category routing. Correlation-only, decays with distance in vector space.

measurement.method: The consult tool boundary: King Wen expanded states + skill cards → Jarvis LLM. Measure: run same payload through Jarvis N times, measure output variance.

edges.notes: Second stochastic boundary. The expanded states + skill cards are the deterministic input; Jarvis LLM produces stochastic output. This is the outer agent boundary where determinism ends.

loader_invariants.description: The 5 v2.0.2 loader invariants, restated for a loader that validates the King Wen edge set.

invariants.enforcement: Every edge's src and dst must reference a node id defined in V. If src or dst is a list (multi-source), all members must be in V.
invariants.example_violation: e_resolved_to_emotional_vector references ir-resolved-9bit — must be defined in V.I

invariants.enforcement: Every edge's operator must be one of the 14 primitives. Custom operators (e.g., EXPAND) must be added to O before use.
invariants.example_violation: Using 'EXPAND' as operator without adding it to O

invariants.enforcement: Every fidelity claim must have a non-empty observation field. 'claimed', 'empirical', 'deterministic' are valid observation bases. A fidelity without observation is not a measurement.
Every determinism claim must have a non-empty basis. 'table-lookup', 'deterministic-algorithm', 'llm-sampling', 'string-formatting' are valid.

invariants.statement: BLOCKED ∉ O (BLOCKED is attempt status, not operator)
invariants.enforcement: No edge may have operator='BLOCKED'. Blocked outcomes are recorded as attempt status, not edge labels.

measurement_framework.description: How to backtest each edge claim. Not all measurements are implemented yet — this is the setup.

measurements.method: Round-trip: 64 hexagrams × 8 phases → ternary → reconstruct binary. Assert bit-exact.
measurements.expected: All 512 round-trips pass (deterministic, reversible when phase_bits known)

measurements.method: Forward: ternary → 9-bit index. Inverse: 9-bit index → ternary. Count collisions (multiple ternary → same index).
measurements.expected: Forward is deterministic. Inverse is lossy (collisions exist) unless full ternary retained.

measurements.method: For each hexagram 1-64, get _primary_pool_for_hex vector. Then: for each vector, find all hexagrams within ε. Count collision sets.
measurements.expected: Many-to-one mapping. Some hexagrams share near-identical vectors (lossy).

measurements.method: For a sample of request texts, run extract_intent → intent_vector. Then: given intent_vector, find texts with same dominant_intent. Measure overlap.
measurements.expected: Deterministic transform, lossy recovery. Many texts → same dominant_intent.

measurements.method: Requires Jarvis runtime. Run same expansion payload through Jarvis LLM N times. Measure output variance.
measurements.expected: Determinism = 0.0. Non-deterministic LLM output. This is the stochastic boundary.

measurements.method: Round-trip: state_key → mobius_gamma → inverse mobius → state_key. Check reconstruction error.
measurements.expected: Möbius is bijective on Riemann sphere. Round-trip should reconstruct within floating-point precision.

measurements.method: Round-trip: state_key → sphere → (u,v) → inverse → sphere. Check inverse_error ≈ 0.
measurements.expected: Stereographic is exact and reversible. inverse_error ≈ 0.

measurements.method: For void hexes 15/20/30/40, run void_null_projection. Check all map to null (radius=0). Inverse: from null, cannot recover which void hex.
measurements.expected: All 4 void hexes map to same null state. Lossy by design.

measurements.method: Run _project_gaussian_future for all 8 phase_bits. Check phase_bias vectors. Inverse: from bias vector, recover phase_bits — check ambiguity.
measurements.expected: Gaussian smoothing makes inverse partially ambiguous. Multiple phases can produce similar bias.

subgraph_state_transitions.description: The kingwen_state_transition.py projector subgraph. These are transformations on state keys, not the base expansion edges. They form a separate subgraph within the IR state-key node.

projectors.notes: Möbius transformation on complex plane; conformal, approximately reversible
Stereographic projection + inverse; exact, fully reversible
Void hexes → null state; lossy by design (4 hexes → same null)
Gaussian-weighted future phase bias; lossy inverse due to smoothing

dispatch.notes: Opcode dispatch maps TransitionOpcode enum to projector function. Mirrors rsmv opcode_reader.ts pattern.
